whatAConfirmationDoesNotCover.judgement: Agreed with the architect, and recorded here so it is a rule rather than one round's care: an unchanged fingerprint does not entail that this branch's deletions survived the merge, and the two must be checked separately. The fingerprint is the branch's diff against its own fork point. A merge that keeps both sides re-adds a paragraph this branch deleted, and since the re-added text is also on the new fork point, the branch's diff against it carries no deletion line for that paragraph either way. The diff is identical whether the deletion survived or not, so the check is structurally blind to exactly the regression this pull request suffered at round three, when the forward merge at 9dae22b7 put back the paragraph defining the pull request body's CI line and the fingerprint said nothing.
